sentences.text: Canadaga is a genus containing only one known species, Canadaga arctica. It was a flightless, toothed seabird belonging to the family Hesperornithidae, which also includes the well-known genus Hesperornis.
Unlike its relatives found in tropical waters, Canadaga seems to have lived in temperate or subarctic areas.
The fossils of Canadaga were discovered in the Kanguk Formation.
Canadaga lived in the shallow seas near modern-day Bylot and Devon Islands in Nunavut, Canada. Fossils of Canadaga date to the Campanian to mid-Maastrichtian age, approximately 67 million years ago.
